t: PCB Layout Generator - Signature build-tool concept
title: PCB Layout Generator - Signature build-tool concept
definition: Places components and routes traces on a printed circuit board.
description:
PCB Layout Generator is the Signature build-tool concept that places components and routes traces on a printed circuit board. In the Signature line, it is not a loose collection of scripts but a deterministic capability: the same build request produces the same verified result on every run, on every machine. This database documents the concept in full - what it is, the seven framework pillars that implement it, the real techniques it stands on, the standards it honors, and laddered drills that teach it from first principles to compounded mastery.

An AI that builds on demand needs PCB Layout Generator the way a workshop needs its central bench. Without it, every build becomes improvisation: requirements drift, steps run out of order, and nobody can say why a result came out the way it did. With it, the build becomes a protocol - inputs declared, transformations explicit, outputs checked against the original request. That protocol is what these records describe, pillar by pillar.

Every record in this database carries a runnable demonstration program, because a build tool that cannot show its work cannot be trusted with real work. Read the overview, study the pillars, practice the drills, and run the demos: by the end the PCB Layout Generator will be a capability you can invoke, not a concept you have read about.

t: Signature Calculator - PCB Layout Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Calculator - PCB Layout Generator framework pillar
definition: The Calculator component of the Signature PCB Layout Generator framework, owning calculator. Signature concept.
description:
The Calculator is a load-bearing component of the Signature PCB Layout Generator framework. Its contract is narrow and absolute: within the framework, everything concerning the framework's calculator responsibilities belongs to the Calculator, and the Calculator answers for it. This separation is what makes the framework testable - the Calculator can be exercised alone, with declared inputs and checkable outputs, long before it is wired into a full build.

In operation the Calculator works like this. A build request arrives carrying the PCB Layout Generator charter (places components and routes traces on a printed circuit board.). The Calculator reads its portion of the charter, performs its transformation, and hands a verified intermediate result to the next pillar. If its checks fail, it stops the line and reports exactly what was wrong, instead of passing corruption downstream. That fail-fast discipline is the Signature line's signature.

Signature-concept illustration: a builder asks for an small electronics job that needs PCB Layout Generator. The Calculator takes the request's calculator responsibilities slice, applies the framework's deterministic procedure, and returns its result with a proof of what it did. Run this record's demo program to see the Calculator's core logic execute on a concrete example - the same logic, the same result, every run.

Signature framing: this pillar is part of the Signature line's original design for PCB Layout Generator. It is labeled a Signature concept throughout - an engineered proposal, not an established public fact. The techniques it relies on are real and cited in the technique records of this database.

t: Signature Draftsman - PCB Layout Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Draftsman - PCB Layout Generator framework pillar
definition: The Draftsman component of the Signature PCB Layout Generator framework, owning draftsman. Signature concept.
description:
Inside the Signature PCB Layout Generator framework, the Draftsman owns the framework's draftsman responsibilities. Frameworks fail when responsibilities blur; the Signature line prevents that by giving each pillar a written contract, and the Draftsman's contract is the sharpest of the seven. It accepts declared inputs, applies one deterministic transformation, and emits a result that any other pillar - or any auditor - can verify independently.

What distinguishes the Signature Draftsman from an ad-hoc script is the verification loop. If the result cannot be justified against the charter, it is rejected and the build halts with a diagnostic instead of a silent wrong answer. Deterministic builds are not a slogan here; they are the acceptance test.

Same seed, same output: that reproducibility is the entire point.

t: Signature Placer - PCB Layout Generator framework pillar
title: Signature Placer - PCB Layout Generator framework pillar
definition: The Placer component of the Signature PCB Layout Generator framework, owning placer. Signature concept.
description:
The Signature PCB Layout Generator framework decomposes the capability (Places components and routes traces on a printed circuit board.) into seven pillars, and the Placer is the one that owns the framework's placer responsibilities. Owning a responsibility means three things in the Signature line: the pillar declares exactly what it accepts, it publishes exactly what it guarantees, and it logs enough evidence that a third party can replay its work and reach the same conclusion.

This discipline pays off when builds go wrong, because they always eventually do. When a PCB Layout Generator result looks suspicious, the auditor does not re-run the whole build and hope; they replay the Placer's log, check its guarantees against its inputs, and find the fault at its source. The pillar is thus both a worker and a witness - it does the work and it testifies about the work.

Try it yourself: this record's demo runs the Placer's core procedure on a worked example. The program is plain JavaScript - save it as demo.js and run it with node, or press Run in the Demo Lab. Change the inputs and re-run; the procedure is deterministic, so you can verify every claim the description makes.
